knowledge.title: NN training: immediate NaN loss or dead flat loss in deep ReLU network — wrong weight init scale; use He init std = sqrt(2/fan_in)
knowledge.solutionUnderTest: 1) Use He/Kaiming init for ReLU-family activations: normal(std=sqrt(2/fan_in)) — torch.nn.init.kaiming_normal_ (PyTorch default for Conv/Linear since 1.0). 2) Xavier/Glorot (sqrt(1/fan_in) or its uniform variant) for tanh/sigmoid. 3) LeakyReLU uses sqrt(2/(1+alpha^2))/sqrt(fan_in). 4) Sanity check: forward one batch through the UNTRAINED net and print activation std per layer — it should stay within roughly [0.5, 2] of the input std at EVERY depth; if layer-20 is ~0 or ~>1e6, the init is wrong. 5) For very deep nets (>~30 layers) add BatchNorm/LayerNorm as the robust fix.

originalProblem.description: The knowledge record EXP-000006 claims that naive weight initialization (std=1.0) causes activation variance to explode exponentially with depth in ReLU networks (NaN or dead loss), while He initialization (std=sqrt(2/fan_in)) keeps variance stable across layers. This claim was verified once with a single check; this run re-verifies it scientifically with controlled experiments, negative controls, boundary conditions and regression tests.
originalProblem.symptoms: deep ReLU networks show NaN loss within the first updates, or a dead-flat loss regardless of learning rate; activation histograms grow/shrink by orders of magnitude with depth
originalProblem.expectedBehavior: forward pass through an untrained deep ReLU network preserves activation scale within roughly an order of magnitude at EVERY depth when weights use He init std=sqrt(2/fan_in); naive std=1.0 explodes by ~fan_in/2 per layer

originalProblem.facts: Var(y) ~ n * E[w^2] * Var(x) for y=Wx with n inputs; ReLU zeroes half the units; He init sets E[w^2]=2/n
